doc.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Joining Woody Herman at twenty and touring Africa
summary: He joined Herman in Fort Worth, toured England and Africa, and had his 21st birthday in Casablanca with Woody.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: You went with Woody Herman at a pretty early age.
That must have been quite an experience. You went overseas?

Yeah. I joined the band in Fort Worth, Texas when I was twenty. I remember it was the day after Christmas and I was absolutely petrified. I flew down there by myself with the bass and joined the band and went to work that night. And it was a great band, Sal Nistico and Bill Chase was on that band, Nat Pierce was playing piano, Ronnie Zito was playing drums. And I went through my growing pains with Woody. I was a kid and very insecure, but I ended up staying — it says in the program I was there for three years, but it was just a year I was there. But during that year we did a lot of one nighters and also did a tour. We went to England and then we also went to a two and a half month tour of Africa, a State Department tour, and we were all over Africa. We were playing in Tanzania, Kampala, Uganda. I had my 21st birthday, actually Woody’s birthday is the same day as mine, and I had my 21st birthday in Casablanca. And Woody bought me a drink and it was one of my good lines that I came up with. Sometimes you think of them but you think about them too late, but I came up with one. He says, “Son, you’ve got a life of misery ahead of ya.” And I said, “I’m not going to stay on the band that long, Woody.” But he loved it, he broke up. But we had, it was Carl Fontana was on that band and there were some great players, and we had a really interesting time in the two and a half months. Very memorable.
